en: a plan designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim; the skill of planning how to achieve success in business, war or politics
ex: The company has a new strategy for entering the Asian market.
公司有一個進軍亞洲市場的新策略。

en: a. carrying or equipped with weapons; having something that protects or helps (e.g. armed with facts); (of a chair) having arms
ex: The police arrested an armed man near the bank.
警方在銀行附近逮捕了一名持械男子。

en: a small amount of water in the air, in the ground, or on a surface; wetness that is found in something such as food or skin
ex: Skin lotion helps keep the moisture in your skin.
護膚乳液有助於鎖住皮膚裡的水分。

en: a. continuing to happen or develop; still in progress; (n.) the process of continuing
ex: The police are in the middle of an ongoing investigation.
警方正在進行持續中的調查。

en: n. a vehicle or weapon shaped like a tube that is pushed into the air by burning gas; a firework; v. to rise very quickly; to move very fast
ex: The rocket was launched from the space center this morning.
火箭今早從太空中心發射升空。

en: a. reasonable and showing good judgment; (of clothes or shoes) practical rather than fashionable; (formal) able to feel or notice something
ex: It would be sensible to take an umbrella with you today.
今天帶把傘會比較明智。

en: a very large amount of money; luck that affects a person's life; the good or bad things that happen to someone
ex: He made a fortune in the stock market before he turned thirty.
他三十歲以前就靠股市賺了一大筆財富。

en: n. a net made by a spider; a complicated system of connected things; the World Wide Web; the skin that joins the toes of ducks and frogs; v. to cover or connect with a web
ex: A spider spun a web between the two branches.
一隻蜘蛛在兩根樹枝間結了網。

en: n. a pipe or channel that carries away water or waste; something that uses up your money or strength; v. to make a liquid flow out of something; to drink all of a drink; to use up all of someone's strength or money
ex: Water flows down the drain after you pull the plug.
拔掉塞子後水會流進排水孔。

en: n. a small gray or red animal with a long thick tail that lives in trees and eats nuts; v. to store something in a safe place for the future
ex: A squirrel was hiding nuts under the tree.
一隻松鼠在樹下藏堅果。

en: n. the joint in the middle of the arm; the part of a sleeve that covers this joint; v. to push someone with your elbow; to push through people
ex: He leaned on his elbow and looked at the screen.
他用手肘撐著，盯著螢幕。

en: v. to speak very quietly using your breath; (of leaves or wind) to make a soft sound; n. a very quiet way of speaking; a rumor; a soft sound
ex: She whispered a secret in her friend's ear.
她在朋友耳邊悄悄說了一個秘密。

en: n. a large shopping area with many stores under one roof; a public area with trees where people walk; (BrE) a wooden hammer used in a game
ex: We spent the whole afternoon at the shopping mall.
我們整個下午都待在購物中心。

en: n. a feeling of coldness; a mild cold illness; a sense of fear or unease; a. rather cold; calm or relaxed; v. to make something cooler; to relax
ex: A chill ran down my spine when I heard the noise.
聽到那個聲音時，我背脊發涼。
ph: send a chill down the spine

en: n. an act that is against religious or moral law; a serious mistake; v. to do something that breaks moral or religious law
ex: Greed is considered one of the seven deadly sins.
貪婪被視為七大罪之一。

en: n. a long narrow piece of cloth, paper or land; a street with many restaurants and shops; v. to take off your clothes; to remove the outer layer of something; to take something away from someone
ex: He cut the paper into thin strips.
他把紙剪成細長條。

en: to try to win or be more successful than someone else; to take part in a race or competition
ex: Many companies compete for the same customers.
許多公司爭奪同樣的顧客。

en: n. an injury to part of the body caused by a cut or blow; an emotional hurt; v. to hurt someone's body or feelings; (past tense of wind) turned or twisted
ex: The nurse cleaned the wound and covered it with a bandage.
護理師把傷口清理乾淨並用繃帶包起來。

en: objects such as rings, necklaces and bracelets that people wear for decoration; (BrE: jewellery)
ex: She keeps all her jewelry in a small wooden box.
她把所有珠寶都放在一個小木盒裡。

en: a. popular at a particular time; following the latest style; used by or used to wealthy and high-society people
ex: Short skirts were very fashionable in the 1960s.
短裙在一九六〇年代非常流行。

en: n. a series of marks for measuring; the size or level of something; a set of musical notes; one of the small flat parts on a fish or snake; (scales) a machine for weighing; v. to climb up something high; to change the size of something
ex: The map has a scale of one to fifty thousand.
這張地圖的比例尺是五萬分之一。

en: n. an animal, especially a large or dangerous one; a cruel or violent person; (informal) something that is difficult to deal with
ex: The beast roared and charged at the hunters.
那頭野獸咆哮著衝向獵人。

en: to depend on someone or something to do what you need or expect; to trust someone
ex: You can rely on me to finish the work on time.
你可以放心由我準時完成這項工作。

en: n. a feeling of surprise and admiration; something that causes this feeling; v. to ask yourself questions about something; to feel surprise and admiration
ex: I wonder what time the store opens tomorrow.
我想知道這家店明天幾點開門。

en: n. a material such as coal, gas or oil that is burned to provide heat or power; something that makes a situation more intense; v. to supply a machine or vehicle with fuel; to make something stronger or worse
ex: The car ran out of fuel on the highway.
那輛車在高速公路上沒油了。

en: n. something wrapped in paper or a bag so that it can be sent by mail; a piece of land; a small part of something; v. to wrap something into a package; to divide something into parts
ex: A parcel arrived at my door this morning.
今早有一個包裹送到我家門口。

en: n. a large hole in the ground; a place where coal is dug; the hard seed in a fruit; (the pits) the area beside a race track for fixing cars; a bad place; v. to set one thing against another
ex: The workers dug a deep pit to bury the old pipes.
工人挖了一個深坑來掩埋舊水管。

en: n. the flat surface of a ship or boat; a floor of a bus or building; a set of playing cards; v. to decorate something; (informal) to knock someone to the ground
ex: We stood on the deck and watched the sun set.
我們站在甲板上看夕陽西下。

en: a large fruit with a hard hairy shell and white flesh and milk inside; the white flesh of this fruit
ex: She drank fresh coconut water on the beach.
她在海灘上喝新鮮的椰子水。

en: the soft part of the body of a person or animal that is between the skin and bones; the soft part of a fruit or vegetable; the human body, especially its physical wants
ex: The cat sank its claws into the soft flesh of his arm.
貓把爪子刺進他手臂柔軟的肉裡。

en: n. a lot of very small drops of liquid sent through the air; a container that sends liquid out in small drops; a small branch with flowers; v. to cover something with small drops of liquid; to shoot a lot of bullets
ex: She sprayed some perfume on her wrist.
她在手腕上噴了一點香水。

en: v. to take something that belongs to someone else without permission; to move quietly and secretly; (baseball) to run to the next base while the pitcher is throwing; n. something bought at a very low price; a theft
ex: Someone stole my bike from the front yard last night.
昨晚有人把我的腳踏車從前院偷走了。

en: a. relating to love or sexual attraction; making you think of love, adventure or excitement; (also Romantic) relating to the art and literature of the Romantic movement
ex: They had a romantic dinner by candlelight.
他們在燭光下享用了一頓浪漫的晚餐。

en: n. a place where two pieces of string, rope or cloth are twisted together; a unit of speed for ships; a hard lump in wood; a tight feeling in the stomach; v. to tie or fasten something with a knot
ex: He tied a knot in the rope so it would not slip.
他在繩子上打了一個結，免得它滑掉。

en: n. fighting between countries or groups using weapons; a long struggle against something bad; a state of competition; v. to fight a war
ex: The country has been at war for more than ten years.
這個國家已經處於戰爭狀態超過十年。

en: n. a hit or knock against something; a raised area on a surface; a small hill or uneven part on a road; v. to hit something with force; to move along a rough surface; to meet someone by chance
ex: The car hit a bump and everyone jumped in their seats.
車子碾過坑洞，大家都在座位上彈了一下。

en: relating to people's race; happening between different races or caused by race
ex: Racial discrimination is against the law in many countries.
許多國家的法律都禁止種族歧視。

en: n. something you must have; the fact that something must happen; a state of being unable to avoid something
ex: Water is a basic necessity of life.
水是生活的基本必需品。
ph: necessity is the mother of invention

en: a. hopeful and confident about the future; expecting good things to happen
ex: She is optimistic about her chances of getting the job.
她對於獲得這份工作的機會很樂觀。

en: n. a person who wears funny clothes and makes people laugh at a circus; a person who behaves in a silly way; (old) a country person; v. to behave in a silly way
ex: The clown made the children laugh with his funny tricks.
小丑用滑稽的把戲逗得孩子們哈哈大笑。
